doc.title: Buddy Burns and Frank Pasley Interview, 1968-09-23

title: Alcorn's cousin George McCullum and a Chicago musician address
summary: They discuss whether McCullum and Alcorn were cousins, Clarence Desdunes's band, and a Jimmy Gordon combo in Chicago.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Those, those, why had to raise up with those boys. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Do you, do you know if he was related to George McCollum Jr.?
Yeah. Cousins. Cousins? Mm-hm. Not half-brothers? Somebody told me they were half-brothers.

Well I know, him and George, George played the trumpet. Yeah I know. Yeah. I thought they were cousins, first cousins myself. A lot of people tried to tell me they were half-brothers or something. I don't know, I got my doubts about that.
But I do know they were some kind of cousins or something.
They played together in Destun's band. Yeah. Do you know Destun's band? Yeah, Sidney. No, not Destwin? No, not Destwin, Clarence Destun.
Oh, Destun, he's from Omaha, isn't he?
Omaha. Yeah. Yeah. But George hasn't played in a long time. Or is he dead? I don't know. He's dead, yeah. George McCullough. Yeah. He was a good trumpet player. Yeah.
Yeah. He was a good reader, I think.
Yeah, yeah. You do. But I think, I think I was better than any of them. Oh, this, yeah.
Yeah. I just seen all of them. He played in Jimmy Gordon's combo? Mm-hmm. I don't, I didn't know. Yeah.
And this blues singer, Jimmy Gordon. I don't know what he is, man.

Yeah. That's a combo. Jimmy Gordon's in saxophone. No, that's like Jimmy Gordon. I don't know what he is, but he says, I will play saxophone in Jimmy Gordon's combo, that's what it says right here. Yeah. But that's where he lives, 6136 Englewood. Probably a different Jimmy Gordon.
